text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/peerage-design-astra.md <<'EOF'
# Source-backed peerage identity design

Recommendation. Add a resolution-run alias context built solely from explicit source bridges. Keep syntax and title recognition in `funder_name`; keep cross-observation ambiguity and identity decisions in declaration resolution. Do not add columns or migrations.

## Grounding

`funder_name.rs` currently owns normalized punctuation-preserving personal names and the single `PersonTitle` vocabulary. `ParsedPersonName` strips recognized leading titles, and `unwrap_given_name` only handles a parenthesized given name before a surname. Consequently `Lord David Sainsbury of Turville` currently yields `david sainsbury of turville`, while the explicit `Baron ... (David Sainsbury)` bridge cannot establish identity.

`ResolutionInput::scoring_input` groups observations into unchanged name/address profiles and unions their blocking keys. `input.rs::blocking_keys` and `identity.rs::classify` both call `individual_donor_name`, whose gate requires donor role and person kind. Scored profile pairs expand back into observation pairs before classification. This is the seam for a shared, computed evidence index. Preserve original comparison names, score probabilities, profile grouping, budget checks, and company/person component restrictions.

## Caller sketch

At validated input construction, derive `PeerageAliases` once from all eligible observations. Both `blocking_keys` and `classify` consult the same per-observation evidence key. The index provides no key for unresolved or ambiguous names.

```rust
let peerage_aliases = PeerageAliases::from_observations(&observations);
// Existing exact person evidence remains independent.
if let Some(key) = input.peerage_aliases.personal_name(&observation.funder_id) {
    keys.insert(format!("peerage-person:{key}"));
}
let peerage_agrees = input.peerage_aliases.agree(&a.funder_id, &b.funder_id);
```

The ordinary personal-name observation must also receive the peerage key when its exact normalized name is one of the index's supported personal names. Otherwise blocking will miss the bridge-to-plain-name pair. `agree` must require two present keys, never `None == None`.

## Ownership and types

In `funder_name.rs`, use a private-field syntax model, for example `PeerageName` with `Style` and `ExplicitBridge` variants, plus exact normalized `PeerageStyle` and `PersonalName` values. The parser accepts raw source and applies the existing normalization. It does not resolve an identity. This can live in a child module if needed for file size, but the module is part of funder-name ownership rather than a competing title parser.

Extend `PersonTitle` with Baron, and any other consciously supported peerage titles, using its canonical `from_token` and an exhaustive title-category match. Do not create another string list of title variants. Avoid broadening titles beyond this task without tests. Equating Lord and Baron here means treating their leading tokens as supported syntactic wrappers around the same exact style, not asserting arbitrary titles identify the same person.

In resolution, `PeerageAliases` owns two-stage collection and ambiguity rejection. A useful private intermediate shape is `BTreeMap<PeerageStyle, BTreeSet<PersonalName>>`. Its stable final surface is an observation-ID-to-supported-personal-name map. It can retain bridge provenance internally if needed for diagnostics. It should not expose a mutable alias registry.

## Parsing contract

Accept an explicit bridge only when the entire normalized source consists of one recognized peerage prefix, a name-like short style with exact ` of ` territory, and one terminal balanced parenthetical full personal name. Reject nested, unmatched, multiple, empty, suffix-bearing or role-bearing parentheses. Trim inner whitespace so `(David Sainsbury )` and `(David Sainsbury)` agree. Reuse the same name-word grammar as current personal parsing rather than duplicating its acceptance rules.

Require the parenthetical name to be a full personal name and require its exact surname suffix to agree with the short style's name portion. This grounds the generated full form in the explicit bridge rather than arbitrary parenthetical text. Initials, conjunctions, representative annotations, trading-as text and unexplained parenthetical labels do not create bridges.

For the valid example, the bridge explicitly supports the personal key `david sainsbury`, short style `sainsbury of turville`, and the generated full style `david sainsbury of turville`. Observation matching remains exact after canonical title stripping and normalization. Do not strip arbitrary `of ...` text, match surnames, or construct combinations from unrelated observations.

## Ambiguity and graph safety

Collect every eligible explicit bridge before emitting any key. A style with more than one distinct personal name is ambiguous for the entire run, independent of observation ordering. Emit no peerage evidence from that style, including for its bridge observations and generated full forms. Repeated agreeing bridges remain usable.

Also collect an exact alias-form-to-target set across the surviving bridges. If one supported form maps to different people, exclude that form instead of selecting the first target. A per-observation key must have exactly one target. This prevents a bridge observation from acquiring multiple personal keys and joining distinct people transitively. Include adversarial tests with shared short styles, multiple styles, collisions between a short style and another bridge's full form, and shuffled input order.

Retain the existing exact-name and existing explicit-trading-alias rules. The guarantee here is that the new peerage rule never creates a link without unique supported evidence. If the desired guarantee is stronger, namely that no existing rule can merge an ambiguous style at all, that is a separate semantic policy change and requires explicit review. Exact identical ambiguous source spellings can still match under existing rules, but must not become a conduit to either inferred personal name through this new context.

## Alternatives

A reviewed durable identity registry makes ambiguity and provenance explicit and could capture titles without in-source bridges. It also adds externally maintained identity data, update lifecycle, persistence and review policy. It is structurally sound but larger than this source-contained bug fix and risks person-specific entries.

Full-form inference could derive `david sainsbury` directly from `Lord David Sainsbury of Turville` and match a surname-based short style. It needs no context, but it turns conventional naming structure into identity evidence and cannot safely distinguish territory/name ambiguities or conflicting holders. Reject it for the requested conservative behavior.

The proposed context keeps the parser pure and puts global knowledge in the owner that already holds all observations. This has a smaller public surface than threading alias arrays through cleaning output, stored features, loaders, scorer schemas and proof fixtures.

## Verification and delivery constraints

Parser tests must cover the exact observed source variants, Unicode and punctuation preservation, malformed and role-bearing annotations, unsupported names and matching surname requirements. Resolution behavior tests must include all five observed variants together with plain David Sainsbury, Lord David Sainsbury and Lord (David) Sainsbury, while Francesca Sainsbury and Francesca Perrin remain separate. Add a generic invented-person fixture proving no hardcoded identity.

Prove missing bridge means no new merge, repeated bridge whitespace means one target, conflicting bridges abstain regardless of order, and organisation/unknown-kind/payer/ultimate-payer observations neither supply nor consume peerage evidence. Test no address or low score is required once exact supported evidence exists, while raw scorer names and probabilities remain unchanged.

Test candidate completeness through the actual blocker/scorer path, not only direct calls to classification with manufactured pairs. Verify the known capture through CLI resolve and entity load against an isolated database, then inspect public funder search/detail HTTP responses to demonstrate a single David identity containing the source spellings and separate Francesca identities. Compare occurrence counts and exact GBP totals before and after to establish attribution conservation.

Check formal verification harness imports before implementation. Harnesses that include resolution source files directly will need the canonical funder-name syntax module and its Unicode dependency, or a small compatible module inclusion. Do not copy the parser or title enum into a harness stub, as that proves different behavior. No new stored field is needed because `Observation.name_raw` is already available at the validated resolution boundary.

Scope risk. Adding Baron to the common title vocabulary changes cleaned personal features for Baron names generally. Include focused regression evidence and regenerate any fixtures or digests tied to feature generation. Existing captures can still use the new context because it parses retained raw values; running cleaning again must not be a hidden prerequisite for this repair.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

Saved design to [/tmp/peerage-design-astra.md](/tmp/peerage-design-astra.md).

Recommend canonical syntax parsing in `funder_name` and a run-wide `PeerageAliases` context owned by resolution. Both blocking and classification consume its unique per-observation personal-name evidence. Retain raw scorer inputs and avoid persistence changes.

Key safeguards include collecting conflicts before emitting aliases, rejecting alias collisions across styles, requiring exact evidence-derived full forms, and testing transitive ambiguity. The document compares registry and full-form-inference alternatives and specifies CLI, load, HTTP, and proof-harness verification.
